request:
Which methods defined directly in the body of the synchronous `Client` class in httpx/_client.py have no docstring? Include private and dunder methods; exclude methods inherited from BaseClient. Give their symbol IDs.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string).
explanation: The query identifies methods directly defined in the Client class body within httpx/_client.py by ensuring their line_start falls after the class definition begins and before the next class definition. It filters to only those methods whose enclosing class is Client (via class_ancestry) and excludes inherited methods. Those without a docstring are detected by the absence of a corresponding 'method' heading record between the class start and the method's line.
sql:
SELECT s.symbol_id
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.files f ON s.file_id = f.file_id
JOIN code.class_ancestry ca ON s.symbol_id = ca.class_symbol_id
WHERE f.file_name = 'httpx/_client.py'
  AND s.kind = 'method'
  AND ca.ancestor_symbol_id IN (
    SELECT symbol_id
    FROM code.symbols
    WHERE file_id = s.file_id
      AND name = 'Client'
      AND kind = 'class'
  )
  AND s.line_start > (
    SELECT MIN(line_start)
    FROM code.symbols
    WHERE enclosing_class_symbol_id IN (
      SELECT symbol_id
      FROM code.symbols
      WHERE file_id = s.file_id
        AND name = 'Client'
        AND kind = 'class'
    )
  )
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM code.headings h
    WHERE h.file_id = s.file_id
      AND h.heading = 'method'
      AND h.value = s.name
      AND h.ordinal > (
        SELECT MIN(ordinal)
        FROM code.headings
        WHERE file_id = s.file_id AND heading = 'class'
      )
      AND h.ordinal < s.line_start
  )
ORDER BY s.symbol_id;
